source_excerpts.text:
For0<e<1, take inactive state0 and a three-state active ring. Each active state
exits to0 at h=1-e;0 enters each active state at e/3. Ring forward and backward
rates are a=2+e/3 and b=1+e/3. This finite CTMC is irreducible. Its stationary
law is pi=(1-e,e/3,e/3,e/3). Each activation edge is detailed-balanced, whereas
the ring has path-KL rate

    sigma_e=e log[(2+e/3)/(1+e/3)] ->0.

Let X_j=1{state=j}-e/3 for the three active states. Exact generator action is
QX=X A^T, with

    A=[[-4,1,2],[2,-4,1],[1,2,-4]],
    Sigma_e=Cov(X)=(e/3)I-(e²/9)11^T.

Sigma_e commutes with A. Whitened observables Y=Sigma_e^(-1/2)X consequently
have Cov(Y(0),Y(t))=exp(A^T t) for EVERY lag, independently of e. A Gaussian OU
with drift A and diffusion D=-(A+A^T)/2 has exactly those covariances. Its
path-KL rate is tr(K^T D^(-1)K)=3/11, where K=(A-A^T)/2. Thus the covariance
Gaussian's positive rate cannot be a universal lower bound on non-Gaussian
path irreversibility. At e=.01 the actual rate is already<.007, while the
matched Gaussian rate is>.27.

The phenomenon also survives the phase-gauge witness at the population level:
the normalized three-channel spectral closure at omega1 has imaginary part
-1639726/190109375, independently checked exactly. A nonzero closure can reject
the reversible covariance null; it does not supply a universal positive
non-Gaussian rate. Since every whitened family member has the SAME complete
covariance function, the infimum valid covariance-only rate floor for that
function is zero.

The identical-covariance statement uses explicitly e-dependent whitening. Its
price is visible: E||Y||^4=9/e-6+e/(1-e), and the inactive waiting time is1/e.
No bounded-amplitude or free acquisition promise is granted. With the FIXED,
bounded raw indicator observables, the Gaussian covariance rate is still3/11:
invertible instantaneous real whitening preserves Gaussian path KL. The raw
covariances then vary with e. These are two different, precisely scoped claims;
the latter basic counterexample does not require unbounded detector outputs.

Consequences: quantitative inference needs a justified Gaussian/physical class
or information beyond these second moments, such as activity/higher moments.
Qualitative time-asymmetry detection and correctly scoped Gaussian inference
remain available. A claim about any particular paper requires reading its
complete theorem and supple

source_excerpts.text:
Input: independent complex three-vectors Z with a specified physical reverse
involution Z->conjugate(Z), optionally with definite scalar parity signs.
Each channel has a fixed nonzero unknown complex gain, stable across replicate
records. Take three independent replicas a,b,c and define

    g=Im[(Z1_a conjugate(Z2_a))
          (Z2_b conjugate(Z3_b))
          (Z3_c conjugate(Z1_c))].

Under channel gains H1,H2,H3, g is multiplied by the POSITIVE factor
|H1 H2 H3|². All sensor phases cancel exactly. Under the physical reverse,
g changes sign; parity signs appear twice and cancel. With centred vectors,
E g is the imaginary covariance closure, but the bound below needs neither
Gaussianity nor centering. Define A=E g and M2=E g²<infinity.

For the three-replica forward law P3 and its reversed law Q3, Q3(g)=P3(-g).
Cauchy–Schwarz gives

    4A² <= [integral (p-q)²/(p+q)] * 2M2.

The pointwise logarithmic inequality gives Jeffreys divergence >= twice that
triangular discrimination. Forward/reverse KL divergences are equal by the
involution, hence D(P3||Q3)>=2A²/M2. Independence makes this

    D(P||P_reverse) >= (2/3) A²/M2.

The ratio cancels the unknown positive gain. This is an implemented per-vector
KL lower bound, not a covariance-only rate formula. The added second moment
of g is a high-order measurement requirement; second covariances do not supply
it. Unknown noise is not automatically reversible or gain-covariant.

## Conditional finite confidence and executed example

If |g|<=G is independently justified and m independent triples are acquired,
normalize z=g/G. The compiler uses exact rational outward radii

    rA>=sqrt(12/m), rM>=sqrt(3/m)

to return (2/3)(|mean z|-rA)_+²/min[1,mean(z²)+rM]. Hoeffding and e^6>400
give simultaneous failure probability<.01. The code verifies e^6>400 by a
rational Taylor partial sum. A maximum observed sample is not a bound G, and
the compiler does not test independence, unclipped gains or sampling laws.

An exact finite-vector fixture has types(1,1,1),(1,i,-1),(1,-i,-1) with
probabilities3/5,3/10,1/10. Optional common uniform phases can make vectors
centred without changing g; those irrelevant phases are analytically eliminated
from the example computation. Exact enumeration of27 type triples gives
A=-6/125,M2=12/25 and per-vector KL floor2/625. The true reverse KL is
(1/5)log3. Unknown example gains(2+i,-1+2i,3-2i) mu
